text: Paddy (rice) field: a familiar Nepali scene containing soil, water, sunlight, rice plants (producers), goats and insects (consumers), and mushrooms and bacteria (decomposers) — a ready-made mixed example for classifying environmental components.
subject: Science

text: Goat: a common domestic animal students see daily; a clear example of a consumer that eats grass and leaves.
subject: Science

text: Mushroom growing on a rotting log during the monsoon: a locally observed decomposer that breaks down dead matter.
subject: Science

text: River or khola water and the stones in it: abiotic components students pass on the way to school; useful to contrast movement (flowing water) with life.
subject: Science

text: Terraced hillside fields, monsoon rain, and morning sunlight: local abiotic conditions that shape which crops and animals live in a place.
subject: Science

text: Temple bell and the madal drum: familiar sound sources for a vibration lesson — striking them and feeling the vibration grounds the idea that sound comes from vibrating objects.
subject: Science
